subject: Post-demo SLO & regional routing plan (FinTrack)
messages:
From: Miguel Soto <miguel.soto@fintrack.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Anika Rao <anika.rao@fintrack.com>
Date: 2026-12-15T14:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Demo today — initial SLO questions

Thanks for the demo earlier — appreciate the flow and the live streaming example. A couple of follow-ups from our side as we gather internal requirements before procurement: 

- Target latency SLOs (for user-facing chat): p50 <= 80ms, p90 <= 220ms, p99 <= 500ms (end-to-end token latency). Can Redwood meet that from EU regions?
- Throughput profile: steady-state ~300 req/s across our EU region during market hours; burst to ~750 req/s for short periods (1-2 minutes) during spikes.
- Concurrency: typical concurrent users ~40 active model sessions, streaming enabled (we need sub-100ms chunk latency for progressive rendering).
- Data residency: EU customer data must remain within EU boundaries (including cache/KV, logs, and any transient data). No cross-border fallbacks except for anonymized telemetry.

We attached our SLO spreadsheet (fintrack-slo-requirements.xlsx) and a brief compliance checklist. Can you confirm: 1) recommended deployment option (Hosted EU vs Dedicated EU vs Private), 2) what routing/fallback behavior you'd propose for multi-region users (APAC/US), and 3) ballpark monthly committed cost for an EU-dedicated pool that meets the above throughput/concurrency?

Short answers are fine — we need to summarize to legal and infra by end of the week.

—Miguel
Head of Platform, FinTrack

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Miguel Soto <miguel.soto@fintrack.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-15T18:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Demo today — initial SLO questions

Thanks Miguel — great questions and thanks for the SLO workbook. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we can give your infra/legal what they need: 

Recap of constraints (from your spreadsheet):
- EU data residency mandatory: all request payloads, KV/prefix cache, and audit logs must stay in EU.
- Live streaming with sub-100ms chunk latency and p99 end-to-end <= 500ms for EU origin.
- Steady-state 300 req/s, burst to 750 req/s, concurrency ~40.
- APAC/US users can be routed to nearest region but EU data must not be replicated outside EU for EU customers.

High-level recommendation (short):
- Deployment: EU Dedicated is our recommended start. It provides predictable throughput, isolated capacity, and can be deployed into your EU VPC (Private connectivity) if needed for audits.
- Routing: Use policy-based routing: origin-based for EU requests (force EU residency), geo-fallback for non-EU requests. For EU-origin requests, strict in-region serving with no cross-border fallback (we can enable a configurable emergency fallback but it requires OA/contractual approval).
- Performance: With Dedicated EU pool sized for 300 req/s steady and burst headroom to 800 req/s (warm pool + autoscale), we expect to meet your p50/p90/p99 targets for typical chat models (with streaming optimizations and prefix caching).

Open items we will confirm with engineering:
1) Exact p99 with streaming enabled for your selected model family at 2.5k context length; we'll run a targeted perf run.
2) Concurrency model (per-session KV memory): estimate warm GPU mem per session and required pool sizing.
3) Audit evidence: confirm SOC2 export window for audit logs stored in EU (we can attach snapshot).

Next steps: 
- We will run a scoped performance qualification in our EU Dedicated test environment — need your sample traffic profile and 48-hour nominal window.
- Vivek will follow up on pricing/commit options for a 6/12 month reserved pool.
- Aditya will propose a simple canary/rollout plan to validate streaming chunk latencies in production.

Can you share a 48hr sample traffic CSV (timestamps + request size + concurrency), and any restricted model families? If convenient, drop in this thread or upload to the Drive link you provided.

Thanks — I’ll loop in Laura (Customer Success) after we have the perf run schedule.

Best,
Monica Patel
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
mobile: +1 (415) 555-0132

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Miguel Soto <miguel.soto@fintrack.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-16T09:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Pricing sketch for EU dedicated capacity

Miguel — looping in pricing so you have a quick-run estimate for legal/budget planning. This is a ballpark based on typical reserved capacity that hits the profile Monica outlined.

Assumptions:
- EU Dedicated pool sized for steady-state 300 req/s, burst headroom to 800 req/s via warm pool + autoscale, concurrency ~40 sessions with streaming enabled.
- Model: open transformer family (4-8B equivalent). If you choose a heavier model, costs scale ~1.6x-2.4x depending on instance sizing.
- Support: Standard SLA; Audit & Compliance add-on (longer log retention + EU KMS) included as a one-time onboarding fee in the quote below.

Estimate (monthly committed):
- Reserved 6-month: EUR 38,000 / month (includes baseline capacity + warm pool + monitoring + 7x24 support inflight for dedicated nodes).
- Reserved 12-month: EUR 32,500 / month (discounted).
- Add-on: Private VPC egress & EU KMS integration: one-time EUR 6,500 setup.

If you want a more precise quote we can size from your 48-hour sample and a chosen model variant. Monica — can we schedule the perf run on EU dedicated infra next Tue/Wed? Aditya, can you outline the canary steps you'll run (traffic split, monitoring, rollback triggers)?

—Vivek
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Miguel Soto <miguel.soto@fintrack.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Anika Rao <anika.rao@fintrack.com>
Date: 2026-12-18T10:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-demo SLO & regional routing plan (FinTrack)

Thanks all — that’s helpful. A few clarifications and asks before we lock the PO: 

1) Canary/rollout: we want a two-week canary in EU with a 5% traffic slice initially, automated rollback on p99 > 750ms or error rate > 0.5% sustained for 3m. Please include those thresholds in the test plan.
2) Emergency fallback: we will not allow cross-border fallbacks for EU-origin requests without a signed exception. Can Redwood flag and alert any attempted fallback in the control plane? We need per-request audit logs showing routing decision and region served.
3) SOC2 snapshot: thanks for the nod — please attach the current SOC2 snapshot and the EU log retention policy. We attached a short acceptance checklist and the perf sample CSV (uploaded to your Drive link).

If you can send the perf-run test plan + canary steps and a refined budget estimate based on the sample by EOD Wednesday, we’ll move to procurement.

Regards,
Miguel
Head of Platform, FinTrack
